projects.title: Firewall Auto-Command Script
projects.description: One of script that I wrote as a Co-op at Ameren, was a script which would login to Firewalls and run user provided commands. I wrote this script in Visual Basic Script, I was told to use this as it does not need any third party software to run and it runs on Windows natively. The script was very simple and easy, I connected to the firewalls using SSH, and for that I used a PuTTY based software called, plink. Plink is a command-line interface to the PuTTY back end. So I was able to execute plink and provide it with lines to run. The user provided two text files. One contained DNS names of firewalls that needed to be logged into to run the commands. Another  contained the login info and the commands to run on the firewalls. The script also created two text log files, one was a history log which contained every line that was outputted to the console and another which was a error log which contained any errors and warnings. With the help of this two log files the user was able to see what went wrong and where it went wrong. The user normally would run the script over night and checked the logs next day to make sure every command had been executed properly. The user that I wrote this script for was pretty happy it had made one of their task a lot easier to accomplish.

projects.title: Car Dash cam
projects.description: I am currently working on my own project to create a dash cam for my car. I am using a Raspberry Pi 3 and a Pi camera module as my hardware right now. I am currently working on the code to record and store video, as well to record the video in small loops. My next part of the project is to design and build my own hardware to a small compact size. Some of the hardware I plan on including, along with the normal hardware, is a G-force sensor, a motion sensor, a sound sensor, a WiFi chip, a video screen, and a Micro SD card slot.
